html:
The founding of the Muslim sultanate of Wadai in eastern Chad about 1635, when Abd al-Karim overthrew the Tunjur rulers of the region.

Wadai grew strong in the 18th and 19th centuries, conquered Bagirmi and controlled a trade route north through the desert to Benghazi, sending slaves, ivory and ostrich feathers. In 1850 the capital moved to Abeche. Wadai's power rested on raiding the peoples of the south for captives, a memory that still divides northern and southern Chad. The French conquered it from 1909, against long resistance. See also Wadai and Kanem-Bornu.
